Hi Emily / Mark —

Thanks again for your time earlier — this thread is a short post-call recap and the proposed implementation / handoff plan so internal teams and your infra team have a clear next step. High-level takeaways from today's discovery: 

- Workload: interactive chat (streaming responses + function/tool calling), embeddings for semantic search, and a reranker that will score 0.5–2k candidate responses for personalization.
- Expected steady-state: ~120 requests/minute during business hours (2/min per user at 60 concurrent users), with burst up to ~600 RPM in peak events. Typical generation responses ~150 tokens; reranker and embedding calls are smaller (~32–256 tokens).
- Latency target: p50 < 250ms for generation (1–150 token responses), p95 target < 600ms.
- Security/compliance: must provide SOC2 evidence and allow Private deployment/networking for production.
- Preferred region: us-west-2.

Recommended next steps (proposed):
1) Technical deep-dive (60m) with NimbleOps infra + Redwood runtime owners — focus on auth, routing, and queueing model (target: week of Jul 6).
2) Share a focused scoping spreadsheet (attached) with traffic weeks + example prompt sizes so we can produce a PoC sizing and cost estimate.
3) Redwood will propose a Dedicated cluster baseline + autoscale policy and an implementation checklist for SDK setup & auth.
4) Procurement ask: draft SOW / PoC pricing to be shared after sizing.

Open items for internal owners:
- Marissa: can you sketch a baseline Dedicated config (gpu count, concurrency per machine, burst plan)?
- Aisha: prepare an SDK auth + service-account walkthrough (preferred pattern for server-to-server, short-lived keys).
- Ben: routing/fallback notes — recommended policy for model variants and queue priorities.

Attachments: nimbleops-scoping-sheet.xlsx (traffic + prompts), redwood-dedicated-arch.png (initial diagram).

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the deep-dive slot once we have availability from NimbleOps.

Emily / Mark — thanks for the quick notes. Short answers up front, then a proposed Dedicated config and follow-ups.

Short answers: 
- Burst / pre-warm: Recommended pattern is baseline Dedicated pool sized for steady state + 1x warm standby for predictable burst. For NimbleOps numbers, baseline = 2 nodes (A40/A100-equivalent) with 1 warm node for 4–5x short bursts, plus autoscale to add X additional nodes if sustained. Warm node is charged but kept paused for fast warm-up.
- Concurrency per GPU: For generation on our optimized runtime expect ~8–12 concurrent streams per A100 for 150-token generation (p50), with p95 rising as concurrency increases. Reranker/embeddings are CPU-light; for reranker we recommend batching to 32–64 items per batch and target ~100–200 qps per GPU for small-token workloads.
- SOC2 + pen-test: We can provide SOC2 artifacts and coordinate the standard external scanning process (redacted report + point of contact). Private deployment (VPC) is recommended for production-sensitive data.

Proposed Dedicated baseline (initial PoC):
- Region: us-west-2
- Model mix: gen-medium (for chat streaming), embedding-small (quantized), reranker-bert-mini (optimized).
- Baseline pool: 2 x A100-equivalent nodes (handles steady-state)
- Warm standby: 1 x A100-equivalent paused-but-warm node for rapid scaling
- Autoscale policy: add 1 node at 60% GPU utilization sustained for 90s, add additional node at each 10% incremental utilization threshold. Scale down after 6 minutes of sustained <30% utilization.
- Concurrency limits: per-node target 10 concurrent gen streams; prioritize reranker/embedding queue with higher priority for low-latency customers (use reserved slots).
- Queuing: Redis-backed request queue with two priority lanes (interactive vs batch), configurable max wait TTL 8s for interactive.
- KV caching: prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts; expect 25–35% token savings for customer workloads with reasonable prompt reuse.

Operational notes:
- Routing/fallback: set a routing policy that falls back from gen-medium -> gen-small (lower cost) if p95 latency breaches target or if capacity constrained. Redwood Console will allow per-route fallbacks.
- SDK/auth: recommend service-account + short-lived tokens (we'll provide an example flow with JWT exchange). Aisha will share the snippet.

Attachments: updated scoping sheet and architecture diagram (redwood-dedicated-arch.png).

Action owners: Marissa to share a cost estimate by Tue Jun 30; Aisha to post SDK auth example; Ben to draft routing policy suggestions.

— Marissa
